newsitem.title: EGYPT: Sudan opposition leaders meet in Cairo.
newsitem.headline: Sudan opposition leaders meet in Cairo.

text.p: Two Sudanese opposition leaders who want to overthrow the Islamic government in Khartoum met in Cairo on Tuesday to discuss the situation in Sudan, a statement by the umbrella opposition National Democratic Alliance said.
Sadeq al-Mahdi and Mohammed Osman al-Mirghani are both in Cairo for talks with Egyptian officials.

It was the first meeting between the two men since Mahdi, former prime minister of Sudan, fled to Eritrea earlier this month saying he wanted to change the government in Sudan with the minimum of bloodshed.

Mahdi met Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa on Monday and explained the opposition's goal to get rid of the Khartoum government. Mahdi was toppled by Lieutenant-Colonel Omar Hassan al-Bashir in a bloodless coup in 1989.
Mirghani, who is chairman of the NDA, held talks with President Hosni Mubarak on Monday.

Mirghani and Mahdi lead the two big traditional parties in northern Sudan, the Democratic Unionists and the Umma Party. Both parties are in the NDA, along with the southern rebels of the Sudan People's Liberation Movement.
The Sudanese opposition in exile has offices in Cairo but its contacts with the Egyptian government are rarely publicised.

Relations between Egypt and Sudan have deteriorated over the past few years with Cairo implicating Khartoum in an attempted assassination of Mubarak in Ethiopia in June 1995 and of sheltering Moslem militants bent on overthrowing the Egyptian government.
Sudan has denied the charges and has lashed out at Egypt for allowing the Sudanese opposition to operate in Cairo.
